newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - NOV 13.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The national economy ministry is planning a practical resolution of problems at the Athens Stock Exchange, with Delta Securities' 2.6 billion drachma default being covered by the depository fund and guarantee fund, and setting tomorrow as a deadline for the clearance of all transactions by brokerage firms or being barred from trading.
--The stock exchange will trade today, brokers say, while, at the same time, a public prosecutor has laid charges of negligence against unnamed officials at the bourse.

--The 1997 budget gets approval amidst disapproval. Yesterday's six-hour inner cabinet meeting was an opportunity for Prime Minister Costas Simitis and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou to hear dissenting opinions on the budget. Final approval, however, was forthcoming.

--Labour costs at Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, shoot up. Internal memo seeks to bring the 40 percent increase in OA spending so far this year down to 20 percent for this two-month period and down another 20 in first quarter 1997.

--An agreement appears possible for the thorny issue of extended trading hours on Saturday. A meeting between merchants, employees and commerce ministry officials looks likely to set 4-5 p.m. as closing time on Saturdays.
IMERISIA

--The bourse will open today as the national economy ministry offers a 'gutless' resolution which does not ensure the settlement of issues on the ASE. Many brokers yesterday expressed their disagreement. Firms of international standing will conduct checks on brokerages.

--The tax scale on bank profits will rise from 35 to 40 percent, the government decides. The decision is expected to be greeted with shock in the banking and credit world, but is a good indication of the government's intentions.This move is considered to be the first in a series being readied to support 1997 budget targets.

--Interior - and former finance - Minister Alekos Papadopoulos proposes a freeze on wage increases at yesterday's marathon inner cabinet meeting. The meeting evenutally decided on 10 basic axes for economic policy, which, sources say, create the conditions for a more competitive environment and fiscal expansion.
--The first package of tax exemption abolitions was also decided by the government: tax on state titles will stand at 7.5 percent and mutual funds taxation will be changed.
KERDOS
--Outflows of 250 million ECU in one day as the crisis on the stock exchange rattles the money and foreign exchange markets, with significant outflows over the past few days.
--The bourse reopens but the problems remain: a one-day deadline for firms to settle transactions or face being barred.
--Five ASE-listed technical firms have given written notice of interest in buying 67 percent of the shares of Kambas wines.
EXPRESS
--Greek brokers return to the bourse after accepting a Papandoniou package.
--The repercussions of the crisis on mutual funds and money markets appear to have been contained.
--Businesses to pay increased taxes as well as losing tax relief, the national economy and finance ministry proposes at yesterday's inner cabinet meeting.
--The final decisions on the budget will be taken at the cabinet meeting next Tuesday, preceded by a ruling party PASOK MPs' meeting on Monday.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--Banks and business face heavier taxes in the storm to come following the abolition of tax relief. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
